This site hosts three independent, self-contained textbooks written from algebraic and combinatorial definitions for competitive programmers who already have a tested algorithm library. Use the top navigation bar or the links below to switch between textbooks; each book maintains its own sidebar navigation, study plan, notation reference, and problem archive.

---

## Textbook I · Formal Power Series & Generating Functions (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

**[Enter the Formal Power Series Textbook →](fps/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](fps/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & 16 Failure Modes](fps/notation.qmd) · [321-Problem Archive](fps/capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd) · [Bibliography & Rosetta Stone](fps/sources.qmd)

A rigorous, zero-forward-reference **6-Part, 24-Chapter** monograph on Formal Power Series ($K[[x]]$, $K((x))$) and Generating Functions for ICPC, Codeforces, AtCoder, and Universal Cup contests:

- **Scope:** Valuation topology $\nu(F)$ and 1D/coupled Newton iteration (`inv`, `sqrt`, `ln`, `exp`, `pow`), $O(NK)$ sparse differential recurrences, the unlabeled ($\operatorname{SEQ}, \operatorname{MSET}, \operatorname{PSET}$) and labeled ($\operatorname{SET}, \operatorname{CYC}$, Boxed Product) Symbolic Method, Bostan–Mori and Berlekamp–Massey, Snake Oil and Stirling/Taylor shifts, roots-of-unity filters and cyclotomic rings, run-length and Goulden–Jackson cluster sieves, online CDQ/relaxed convolutions, formal Laurent residues and 6-form Lagrange Inversion, cactus/block-cut/DAG/SCC graphical series, stochastic PGFs, 1D/2D kernel methods, the 5-ring bivariate hierarchy and Furstenberg diagonals, D-finite ODEs and $p$-adic indicial lifting, Tellegen transposition (`mulT`, multipoint `eval`/`interp`), Kinoshita–Li $O(N \log^2 N)$ `power_projection`/`compose`/`revert`, Static Top Tree DP, $q$-analogues, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$.
- **Practice & Assessment:** **192** inline chapter ladder problems (`2 Stepping Stones`, `2 Intermediate`, `2 Advanced`, `2 Mastery` per chapter), **6** Two-Stage Blind Topic-Group Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](fps/checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)–[`CP-VI`](fps/checkpoints/cp06-part6-trees-qseries-sps-dirichlet.qmd), 48 problems), and a **14-problem** [Multi-Perspective Synthesis Reserve](fps/capstones/synthesis-reserve.qmd) (`Syn-01`–`Syn-14`).
- **Start here:** [FPS Overview](fps/index.qmd) or directly at [Ch 01 · The Ring $K[[x]]$, Valuation Topology & Newton Inversion](fps/chapters/ch01-ring-convolutions-newton-inv.qmd).

## Textbook II · Network Flows, Minimum Cuts, Matching, Duality & Modelling (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

**[Enter the Network Flows & Modelling Textbook →](flows/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan & 3-Axis Diagnostic](flows/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & 24 Failure Modes](flows/notation.qmd) · [320-Problem Archive](flows/capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd) · [Bibliography & Rosetta Stone](flows/sources.qmd)

A rigorous, zero-forward-reference **6-Part, 24-Chapter** modelling-first monograph dedicated to recognizing hidden flow, minimum-cut, matching, and LP-dual structures in problem statements with **no graphs mentioned at all** (`Direction A: Non-Graph -> Flow`) and eliminating flow solvers into $O(N \log N)$ algorithms when $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ (`Direction B: Flow -> Fast Algorithm`):

- **Scope:** Flow-cut duality, Picard–Queyranne residual condensation DAGs, feasible vs. essential cut edges (`[AHOI2009]`), incremental flow rollback (`退流`, `[SDOI2014] LIS`), vertex/time splitting, lower-bound circulations (`上下界网络流`) and Hoffman's theorem, König–Hall–Dilworth duality, Dulmage–Mendelsohn (`DM`) decomposition and bipartite walk games, Birkhoff–von Neumann and regular edge coloring (`AGC 037 D`), segment-tree Hall Marriage elimination (`ARC 076 F`), Maximum Weight Closure (`最大权闭合子图`), submodular pseudo-Boolean cut compilation (`燃やす埋める`), Bipartite Variable Inversion (`二部グラフの片側反転`, `AGC 038 F — Two Permutations`), multi-state unary threshold chains and disjunctive OR cuts (`ARC 107 F — Sum of Abs`, `ARC 142 E — Pairing Wizards`), Ishikawa convex Monge penalties, the Discrete Coarea Formula (`CF 1427 G — One Billion Shades of Grey`), 0-1 fractional programming (`Dinkelbach`), Maximum Density Subgraphs, planar $s$-$t$ and $k$-terminal dual shortest paths (`[NOI2010] 海拔`, `[CSP-S 2021] 交通规划`), min-cut DP (`CF 724 E`, `CF 1919 F2`), Gomory–Hu cut trees, MCMF Johnson potentials, negative-cycle saturation, convex marginal edge splitting, Consecutive Equation Differencing (`[NOI2008] 志愿者招募`), cycle covers, dynamic scheduling, coordinate-rank slots (`AGC 031 E`), Manhattan $2^d$ hubs (`AGC 034 D`), explicit LP duality, Totally Unimodular (TU) matrices, DS-accelerated flow graphs (`线段树/主席树优化建图`), Edmonds' Blossom and Tutte matrix, Simulated MCMF (`模拟费用流 / 反悔贪心`), and $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`).
- **Practice & Assessment:** **192** inline chapter ladder problems (`#001`–`#192`, each compiled via the **4-Step "Zero Magic Gadgets" Standard**), **6** Part-End Blind Recognition Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](flows/checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)–[`CP-VI`](flows/checkpoints/cp06-part6-ds-blossom-simulated-isotonic.qmd), `#193`–`#240`), and a **16-problem** [Grandmaster Synthesis Reserve](flows/capstones/synthesis-reserve.qmd) (`#241`–`#256`).
- **Start here:** [Network Flows Overview](flows/index.qmd) or directly at [Ch 01 · Conservation Laws, Residual Graphs, and Max-Flow Min-Cut Duality](flows/chapters/ch01-conservation-residual-maxflow-mincut.qmd).

## Textbook III · Competitive Programming Mathematics (`00`–`20`)

**[Enter the Competitive Programming Mathematics Textbook →](math/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan (`00`–`20`)](math/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & Contracts](math/notation.qmd) · [Sources & Policy](math/sources.qmd)

A broad **21-Chapter** foundation and synthesis curriculum covering the general mathematical pillars of competitive programming from first principles:

- **Part I · Arithmetic and counting (`00`–`05`):** [Foundations and proof](math/00-foundations/chapter.qmd), [modular algebra](math/01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd), [multiplicative number theory](math/02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd), [combinatorics](math/03-combinatorics/chapter.qmd), [binomials modulo anything](math/04-modular-binomials/chapter.qmd), and [group actions (Burnside/Pólya)](math/05-group-actions/chapter.qmd).
- **Part II · Algebraic engines (`06`–`11`):** [Polynomials and FFT/NTT](math/06-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [linear algebra](math/07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd), [subset and divisor transforms](math/08-transforms/chapter.qmd), [formal power series overview](math/09-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd), [generating functions overview](math/10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd), and [set power series](math/11-set-power-series/chapter.qmd).
- **Part III · Models and synthesis (`12`–`15`):** [Probability and Markov chains](math/12-probability/chapter.qmd), [discrete sums and floor geometry](math/13-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd), [summatory sieves](math/14-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd), and [mixed capstones](math/15-capstones/chapter.qmd).
- **Part IV · Frontier topics (`16`–`20`):** [$q$-analogues and subspaces](math/16-q-analogues/chapter.qmd), [finite-field polynomials](math/17-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [algebraic graph methods (Pfaffians/Tutte)](math/18-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd), [holonomic methods](math/19-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd), and [frontier capstones](math/20-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd).
- **Start here:** [Mathematics Overview](math/index.qmd) or directly at [00 · Mathematical foundations and proof](math/00-foundations/chapter.qmd).

## Which Textbook Should You Read?

| Your Goal | Recommended Entry Point |
| :--- | :--- |
| Master generating functions, polynomial operators, tree/graph enumeration, bivariate diagonals, ODEs, or Set Power Series in depth | **[Textbook I · Formal Power Series (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](fps/index.qmd)** |
| Recognize hidden flow/min-cut/matching/MCMF models in non-graph problems (`燃やす埋める`, `切糕`, LP duality, `模拟费用流`, `保序回归`) | **[Textbook II · Network Flows & Modelling (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](flows/index.qmd)** |
| Build general foundations in proof, modular arithmetic, number theory, linear algebra, probability, and sublinear sieves | **[Textbook III · Competitive Programming Mathematics (`00`–`20`)](math/index.qmd)** |
